questions.q: A transparent block A having refractive index $\mu=1.25$ is surrounded by another medium of refractive index $\mu=1.0$ as shown in figure. A light ray is incident on the flat face of the block with incident angle $\theta$ as shown in figure. What is the maximum value of $\theta$ for which light suffers total internal reflection at the top surface of the block?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{r}+\theta_{\mathrm{C}}=90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \\ & \mu_1 \sin \theta=\mu_2 \sin \mathrm{r} \\ & \sin \theta=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \sin \left(90-\theta_{\mathrm{C}}\right) \\ & \sin \theta=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \cos \theta_{\mathrm{C}} \\ & \sin \theta_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \sin \theta=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \sqrt{1-\frac{\mu_1^2}{\mu_2^2}} \\ & \sin \theta=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_2^2-\mu_1^2}{\mu_1^2}}=\sqrt{\frac{\frac{25}{16}-1}{1}} \\ & \sin \theta=\frac{3}{4} \\ & \theta=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Light enters from air into a given medium at an angle of $45 °$ with interface of the air-medium surface. After refraction, the light ray is deviated through an angle of $15 °$ from its original direction. The refractive index of the medium is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $i = 45 °$

Deviation in light ray,~$D = i - r$, here,~$r$~is refracted ray.

$⇒ 15 ° = 45 - r ⇒ r = 30 °$

Using Snell's law,

${n}_{1}sini = {n}_{2}sinr$

$⇒ 1\sin 45 ° = \mu sin30 °$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \mu\dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, the~refractive index of the medium is~$\mu = \sqrt{2} = 1 . 414$

questions.q: The eye can be regarded as a single refracting surface. The radius of curvature of this surface is equal to that of the cornea $( 7 .8 mm )$. This surface separates two media of refractive indices $1$ and $1.34$. Calculate the distance from the refracting surface at which a parallel beam of light will come to focus.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know eye lens is convex refracting surface.

Use expression for refraction from curved surface



${\mu}_{1} \to$ Refractive index of medium having incident ray

${\mu}_{2} \to$ Refractive index of a medium having reflected ray

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{2}}{v} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{u} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}$

$\dfrac{1.34}{v} - \dfrac{1}{\infty} = \dfrac{1.34 - 1}{7.8}$

$v = 30.7mm$

$v = 3.07cm$

questions.q: If the refractive index of the material of a prism is $\cot \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right), where $A$ is the angle of prism then the angle of minimum deviation will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the refractive index \left(\mu\right)$ of the material of the prism is given by

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{A + {δ}_{m}}{2}\right)}{\sin \left(\dfrac{A}{2})} . . . \left($1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$cot\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{A + {δ}_{m}}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ cos\dfrac{A}{2} =$\sin \left(\dfrac{A + {δ}_{m}}{2}\right)⇒ \sin \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}) ==\sin \left(\dfrac{A + {δ}_{m}}{2}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{A + {δ}_{m}}{2} = \dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}

$⇒ {δ}_{m} = $\pi -$2A$

questions.q: A plano-convex lens having radius of curvature of first surface 2 cm exhibits focal length of $f_1$ in air. Another plano-convex lens with first surface radius of curvature 3 cm has focal length of $\mathrm{f}_2$ when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.2 . If both the lenses are made of same glass of refractive index 1.5 , the ratio of $f_1$ and $f_2$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For case (1)
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1.5}{v_1}-\frac{1}{\propto}=\frac{(1.5-1)}{R_1} \\ & \frac{1}{f_1}-\frac{1.5}{v_1}=\frac{1-1.5}{\propto}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f_1}=\frac{(1.5-1)}{R_1}$ ...(1) $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{f_1}=\frac{1}{2 R_1}$ For case (2) $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1.5}{v_1}-\frac{1.2}{\infty}=\frac{(1.5-1.2)}{R_2} \\ & \frac{1.2}{f_2}-\frac{1.5}{v_1}=\frac{(1.2-1.5)}{\propto} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1.2}{f_2}=\frac{0.3}{R_2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{f_2}=\frac{1}{4 R_2} \end{aligned}$ So clearly, $\frac{f_1}{f_2}=\frac{2 \times 2}{4 \times 3}=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.q: A convex lens has power $P$. It is cut into two halves along its principal axis. Further one piece (out of the two halves) is cut into two halves perpendicular to the principal axis (as shown in figures). Choose the incorrect option for the reported pieces.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Lens maker's formula, power is given by

$P = \dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu -1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R1} - \dfrac{1}{R2}\right)

~

When convex lens is cut into two parts,~${P}_{1} = $\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu -$1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{R}\right) =$P$

~

When half convex lens is cut into two parts,${P}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu -$1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right) = \dfrac{P}{2}

Power of lens, ${P}_{3} = $\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu -$1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}) = \dfrac{P}{2}

questions.q: Critical angle of incidence for a pair of optical media is $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$. The refractive indices of first and second media are in the ratio:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin \theta_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\mu_{\mathrm{R}}}{\mu_{\mathrm{d}}}=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \\ & \sin 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A convex lens (of focal length $20$ cm ) and a concave mirror, having their principal axes along the same lines, are kept $80$ cm apart from each other. The concave mirror is to the right of the convex lens. When an object is kept at a distance of $30$ cm to the left of the convex lens, its image remains at the same position even if the concave mirror is removed. The maximum distance of the object for which this concave mirror, by itself would produce a virtual image would be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Image formed by lens
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30}$
$⇒ v = 60cm$
In the image remains at the same position even if the concave mirror is removed indicates that the image formed by lens is formed at the center of curvature of spherical mirror.
$∴$ Radius of curvature of mirror $= 80 - 60 = 20cm$
Focal length, $f = 10cm$
For virtual image to be formed, object is to be kept between focus and pole. Hence, the maximum distance of object from spherical mirror for which virtual image is formed will be its focal length 10cm

$\begin{aligned} & \text { Using } m=\frac{f}{u-f} \\ & m_1=\frac{6}{18-6}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{m}_2=\frac{6}{18+6}=\frac{1}{4} \quad \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~m}_2}{\mathrm{~m}_1}=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.q: A thin lens made of glass (refractive index $= 1.5$ ) of focal length $f = 16cm$ is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.42$ . If its focal length in liquid is ${f}_{l}$ , then the ratio ${f}_{l} / f$ is closest to the integer:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
\dfrac{1}{{f}_{a}} = \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{g}}{{\mu}_{a}} -$1\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{m}} = \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{g}}{{\mu}_{m}} -1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}})
$⇒ $\dfrac{{f}_{a}}{{f}_{m}} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{g}}{{\mu}_{m}} - 1\right)}{\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{g}}{{\mu}_{a}} - 1\right)} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1.50}{1.42} - 1\right)}{\left[\dfrac{1.50}{1} - 1\right]} = \dfrac{0.08}{\left(1.92\right)\left(0.5\right)}
\dfrac{{f}_{a}}{{f}_{m}} = \dfrac{\left(1.42\right)\left(0.05\right)}{0.08} =$8.875 \approx 9$$

questions.q: A slanted object $A B$ is placed on one side of convex lens as shown in the diagram. The image is formed on the opposite side. Angle made by the image with principal axis is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Location of image of $\mathrm{A}:-$
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-30}=\frac{1}{20} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{1}{60} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=60 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{~m}=2\end{aligned}$
Since size of object is small wrt the location hence
$\begin{aligned} & d v=m^2 d u \Rightarrow d v=4 \times 1=4 \mathrm{~cm} \\ & h_i=m h_0 \Rightarrow h_i(d y)=2 \times 2=4 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
$\therefore$ Angle made with principle axis $=-45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$

questions.q: A light wave is incident normally on a glass slab of refractive index $1.5 .$ If $4%$ of light gets reflected and the amplitude of the~electric field of the incident light is $30\dfrac{V}{m},$ then the amplitude of the electric field for the wave propagating in the glass medium will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$n =$~refractive index ~ $= \sqrt{{ε}_{r}{\mu}_{r}}$
$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2}C$

$I^{′} = \dfrac{1}{2}εE^{2}V$

$I^{′} = 0.96I$

$\dfrac{1}{2}εE^{2}v = 0.96\dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2}C$

$E = \sqrt{0.96}\sqrt{\dfrac{{ε}_{0}}{{ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}}}\sqrt{\dfrac{c}{v}}{E}_{0}$

(For most of the transparent medium ${\mu}_{r} \approx 1$ )
~ $⇒ E = \sqrt{0.96} . \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{ε}_{r}{\mu}_{r}}} . \sqrt{\dfrac{c}{v}}{E}_{0}$

$= \sqrt{0.96} . \dfrac{1}{n} . \sqrt{n}{E}_{0}$

$E = \sqrt{\dfrac{0.96}{n}}{E}_{0}E = \sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 96}{1 . 5}} \times 30 = 24\dfrac{V}{m}$

questions.q:
A convex lens of refractive index $1 . 5$ and focal length $18$ cm~in air is immersed in water. The change in focal length of the lens will be_____cm$.~

(Given refractive index of water$= \dfrac{4}{3})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Lens Maker's formula,

For air:& $\dfrac{1}{fa} = \left(\dfrac{\mug}{\mua} -1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R1} - \dfrac{1}{R2}\right)

For water:~\dfrac{1}{fw} = \left(\dfrac{\mug}{\muw} -1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R1} - \dfrac{1}{R2}\right)

$∴ $\dfrac{1{f}_{a}}{1{f}_{w}} = \left(\dfrac{\mug}{\mua} -$1\right) \left(\dfrac{\mug}{\muw} -1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{fw}{fa} = \left(1 . 5 - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1 . 5 \times 3}{4} -1\right) ⇒ {f}_{w} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{0 . 125} \times18 = 72cm$

Thus, change in focal length of the lens is~$72 - 18 = 54cm$

$

questions.q: A light ray is incident, at an incident angle ${θ}_{1}$, on the system of two plane mirrors ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ having an inclination angle $75 °$ between them (as shown in figure). After reflecting from mirror ${M}_{1}$ it gets reflected back by the mirror ${M}_{2}$ with an angle of reflection $30 °$. The total deviation of the ray will be _____ degree.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the above figure,& ${i}_{2} = 30 °$,

Now,~

$∠ OBA + ∠ ABR + ∠ RBP = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OBA + 60 ° = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OBA = 60 °$

In triangle~$OAB$,

$∠ OBA + ∠ AOB + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ 60 ° + 75 ° + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OAB = 45 °$

And,

$∠ OAB + ∠ BAI + ∠ IAQ = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OAB + 2{i}_{1} = 180 ° ⇒ {i}_{1} = 45 °$

Now the total deviation of the ray will be,

$\delta = 360 ° - 2\left({i}_{1} + {i}_{2}\right) ⇒ \delta = 360 ° - 2\left(30 ° + 45 °\right)\delta = 210 °$
